title: Rebuild
author: William Saville
content:
Wind screams,
As the avalanche falls,
Gusts of snow,
Upon hills and walls.
The town looks in horror,
The people scatter,
The safety is gone,
Hopes did shatter.
The ache and pain,
A way of life diminished,
Flee to another place,
As this one is finished.
The sun rises,
And sets each day,
On and on,
It's pattern won't sway.
Not everyone's natural disaster,
Is a physical thing,
Taking lives and homes,
With chaos bring.
But sometimes it's smaller,
Like a word spoken,
Or a slap to the face,
Or a promise broken.
No matter your disaster,
It's valid and true,
Whatever ails your heart,
It's everything to you.
Like a town you can be rebuilt,
There is no need to flee,
Your walls might be shaken or broken,
But you can make a decree.
By your lonesome or with others,
You can take it brick by brick,
Rebuild yourself and flourish,
There is no need to be quick.
Just make sure to build a door,
To those strong walls you build,
For those who earn your trust,
To walk through with hope fulfilled.
